brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.requirement: A base structure for the organizer
requirements.evidence: Hex base pieces: full piece at (0,0), full piece at (1,0), and half-e piece at (-1,0), held together by joint bolts at (0,0) and (-1,0).
Bin hex-bin-full at (0,0) and hex-bin-full-div2 (2-compartment) at (1,0). Both are drop-in trays that lift out of their cells.
Slide drawer 'w' (drawer:0#-1,0#cut) on the cut face of half-e base at (-1,0). Also a drawer-frame notch at (0,1) (notch1) is present but no drawer is fitted into it.
Handle handle:0,0,0;top on the top cover (cover:0,0,0;full;top) of the base at (0,0), with three inserts.
Compact build of 3 base pieces, 2 bins, 1 drawer, 1 handle; check_build reports meshClash clear and no rule errors. Fit only was checked; weight and strength were not assessed.

finish.summary: Built a small portable organizer: three base blocks joined by two joint bolts, a top cover with carry handle at the origin cell, a full bin and a 2-compartment bin for small parts, and a slide drawer on the half-base cut face. check_build is clear (meshClash clear, only an informational open-cap note). An unfilled drawer-frame notch remains at (0,1); it is harmless but could be removed. Portability is by size and handle only; weight and load were not evaluated.

M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
